Notes

A producer’s name becomes a friend’s martial-arts legend. Modesty, a backpack and an ordinary platform keep the grandiose portrait close enough to everyday life to be funny.

三毛

The friend’s name 三毛 is Sānmáo; the official production credit for this track is 3MAO. That puts the name inside an actual creative partnership before the verse inflates it into a martial-arts legend. The credit explains the connection, while the improbable combat portrait works as playful mythmaking around the named figure.

  • Jack Zebra: official Zhuang Zhuang track list
空手道

空手道 is karate-dō, literally the “way of the empty hand.” The name gives a compact explanation for the previous boast that Sanmao does not need to carry a knife. The next emphasis on technique rather than strength also keeps the portrait focused on acquired skill.

  • Chinese lyric transcript (Genius community)
  • Japan Karate Association: meaning of karate-dō
只背了一个书包

书包 is a school-style bag or backpack, a strikingly modest item for someone arriving with lethal combat skills. 只, “only,” emphasizes how little luggage he needs. Along with the admission that he is not very strong, the image builds an unshowy exterior that the later “god of kung fu” will spectacularly exceed.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
谦虚低调

谦虚 praises not boasting; 低调 praises keeping a low profile. The narrator, however, does plenty of boasting on the fighter’s behalf. That division is the joke’s engine: Sanmao can remain solemn and modest while a friend supplies the apocalyptic reputation, the anxious spectators and the title of kung-fu god.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
开始录像

“Start recording” turns the listener from a recipient of the tale into a potential spectator with a camera. Later the narrative shifts from “he” to “we” applauding: the scene is as concerned with witnessing the fighter as with the fight itself.

  • Chinese lyric transcript (Genius community)
唯一信仰

信仰 is faith or a sustaining belief, so treating victory as its only object gives competition the seriousness of a creed. It also cuts against the friendly introductory “I have a friend.” The portrait gradually shifts from anecdote to heroic legend through the vocabulary around him, not through a detailed account of any particular move.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
站台

After war, faith and a martial-arts god, the applause happens on a platform. That plain transport setting brings the action back within everyday public life instead of ending in a temple or arena. The narrator’s “we” also makes the legend collective: a group has been watching and now certifies the victory by applauding.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)
安静

The closing command cuts off the applause the story has just created. It can address the gathered spectators and the listener at once: after narrating the friend’s power, the voice also directs the room’s response. That small act of crowd control caps a song full of looking, recording, tension and public recognition.

  • Lyric transcript (the passage discussed here)

About Jackzebra and this mixtape

Zhuang Zhuang Mixtape arrived on Surf Gang on October 2, 2026: 55 tracks, opening with Sour and closing with Sweet. Its cast widens from YoungQueenz on Poker Face to User116, Effie, kuru, yoyi, 春 and 南部犯罪份子. Aghast has a production credit on every track from Hitman through Snatch, giving that stretch a shared collaborator behind its changing scenes.

Surf Gang release · Artist credits

Jackzebra told AVYSS that he writes while singing over a beat he has listened to repeatedly, keeping the images in his head central. He values the room Mandarin leaves for indirect meanings. Listen for ordinary phrases becoming physical scenes: familiarity becomes cooking, authority becomes family seniority, and a tired saying suddenly turns into a threat.

AVYSS interview, 2024

In STATIC, he describes mixtapes as a format for letting ideas flow, reserving an official debut album for later. In a separate conversation about Above & Beyond, he compared that earlier tape to a collection of his producer friends’ work. The credits here likewise reward attention: long-running collaborators sit alongside guests working in Mandarin, Korean and English.

STATIC interview · Sabukaru interview, 2025

The small details connect to his stated interests: he has described playing Temple Run in transit and before shows, watching Top Boy, and wanting to score White Oleander. These give the songs specific points of contact with his life. The notes follow those connections alongside the lyrics’ jokes, invented scenes and competing voices.

His recommendations in Perfectly Imperfect · Dazed interview, 2025 · Interview questionnaire, 2025

Jackzebra has pushed back on being made to represent all of China’s underground. These notes stay close to the words: what an expression usually means, what changes in this line, and how another song answers it. Cultural references have sources; interpretations rest on details you can hear or read in the song.
